eval.description:
Tests if a workspace lens can read the middle step that a model computes but does not say.

Each item is a prompt with a known hidden token. For example, to answer "the organ that pumps blood has this many chambers" with "4", the model must think of "heart". The lens reads the model at one set token of the prompt, at seven layers spaced through the model. An item is a hit when the hidden token is in the lens's top 10 tokens at one layer or more. Before the top 10 is taken, tokens with no letter or digit are dropped (Readout Filtering).

The five tasks are multihop, multilingual, typo, association and poetry. The headline score is the mean recall@10 over the tasks.

Gurnee et al. (2026) made the items and the metric. Ayonrinde and Lindsey adapted them for the J++ Lens paper.
eval.summary: Tests if a workspace lens reads the hidden middle step of a task from a model's activations.

versions.changes:
New runs of the 2026-10.2 setup on the six models, with one change to the readout token.

- **Readout token:** a prompt that ends in a space is now read without the space, at the token before the answer. Most tokenizers join the space to the next word (" Portuguese"), so in 2026-10.2 the lens read a lone space token. This applies to 168 prompts with a word answer (52 multihop, 19 multilingual, 97 poetry). For poetry, the readout stays at the line break, so only the model's grade changes.
- **Number answers:** the 31 multihop prompts with a number answer keep the space. All six tokenizers split the space from a number, so the space is the token before the answer.
- **Check:** for each changed prompt, the run stops with an error if the prompt does not end at the token before the answer in the tokens of prompt + answer.
- **J++ Lens:** we use the same Neuronpedia J++ Lens files. Their expert weights were fit with the space token as the readout, so they can be a bit worse at the new readout token.
- **Effect:** on five models, scores are 0.7 to 3.4 points higher than in 2026-10.2, mostly from multihop (up to 11 points) and multilingual (up to 11 points). The one drop is the J++ Lens on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (0.6 points; 6 points on multihop), which can come from its expert weights. The J++ Lens is still first on all six models.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash:** this run is on two H200s, not four RTX PRO 6000s. Its 8-bit kernels give slightly different ranks on other GPUs, so tasks with no changed prompt also move, by up to 2.5 points. Its scores move by -0.4 to +1 points.

The items, the fit split, the lenses and the other notes are the same as in 2026-10.2.

versions.changes:
The same runs as 2026-10.1, with no correctness filter.

- **All answers count:** an item counts also when the model answers it wrong. The test is of the lens, not of the model, and neither paper gives a reason for the filter. The filter also drops a different set of items for each model. Gemma 4 31B now has all five tasks.
- **Fit items:** the items that the J++ Lens fit used still do not count, for all lenses. This is 20% of the items that pass the filter.
- **Readout token:** as in the harness, a prompt that ends in a space is read at the space token. For the 168 prompts with a word answer, this is not the token before the answer, because the tokenizer joins the space to the word.
- **Effect:** scores are 0 to 9 points lower than in 2026-10.1, and 7 to 10 points lower for Gemma 4 31B, which now has poetry. The J++ Lens is still first on all six models.

The lenses and the other notes are the same as in 2026-10.1.

versions.changes:
OpenAudit's own runs of the paper's harness ([jpp_lens](https://github.com/safety-research/jpp_lens) at `d7efc0de`) on the paper's six models. The items, the seven layers and Readout Filtering are the same as the paper's.

- **Correctness filter:** an item counts only when the model answers it right. Typo and association items always count. We graded the answers with the harness, and our grades for Qwen3.6-27B are the same as the paper's. Gemma 4 31B has no poetry score, because only 1 of its 98 items passes.
- **Lenses:** the J++ Lenses are from Neuronpedia, and the R-Lenses are our fits. Both use 64 WikiText-103 prompts. The J-Lenses are from Neuronpedia (456 to 1,000 WikiText prompts), or from Camila Blank (25 Pile prompts) on the Qwen3.5 models and DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash:** it runs on its own 8-bit weights. It uses Camila Blank's R-Lens, because our fit needs the bf16 model (about 570 GB).
- **Not comparable with 2026-10:** most of our scores are higher than the paper's, also for the logit lens, which has no fit. With the paper's R-Lens files, our scores are 4 to 7 points higher on the Qwen3.5 models. So the differences come from the eval runs, not from the lens fits.
- This version has no swap test.
